rationale: Salsa20 is a stream cipher whose security-critical work sits in a very hot quarter-round loop over small, compute-dense functions, so the weight table favors low-cost data-level transforms and penalizes control-flow heavy passes on the hot path. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain with low cost/risk weights because instruction substitution obscures the ARX arithmetic without materially hurting the tight loop; SPLIT is cheap and composes well, aiding diversity at negligible overhead. FLA and BCF have strong obfuscation value but heavy runtime/size footprints, so their high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights suppress their application to the cipher's hot functions while still allowing selective use on cold setup/key-schedule code; FLA also carries a modest CorrectnessRisk weight since flattening loop-heavy crypto kernels can disturb optimization. IBR is kept as a moderate option for hiding branch structure but with elevated RuntimeCost weight to keep it off the innermost loop. ICALL and IGV are down-weighted because salsa20 is a self-contained kernel with few indirect calls and globals, so they add call/lookup overhead and risk for little gain.
